---
title: Route Segment Config
description: Learn about how to configure options for Next.js route segments.
---

The Route Segment Config options allow you to configure the behavior of a [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) by directly exporting the following variables:

| Option                                                                                             | Type                                                              | Default                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams)     | `boolean`                                                         | `true`                     |
| [`runtime`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/runtime)                 | `'nodejs' \| 'edge' (deprecated)`                                 | `'nodejs'`                 |
| [`preferredRegion`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/preferredRegion) | `'auto' \| 'global' \| 'home' \| string \| string[] (deprecated)` | `'auto'`                   |
| [`maxDuration`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/maxDuration)         | `number`                                                          | Set by deployment platform |

## Version History

| Version      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v16.0.0`    | `dynamic`, `dynamicParams`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` removed when [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled. See [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#route-segment-config). |
| `v16.0.0`    | `export const experimental_ppr = true` removed. A [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-experimental_ppr-route-segment-config-from-app-router-pages-and-layouts) is available.                                                                                                  |

00002| title: unstable_noStore
00003| description: API Reference for the unstable_noStore function.
00004| version: legacy
00005| ---
00006| 
00007| **In version 15, we recommend using [`connection`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) instead of `unstable_noStore`.**
00008| 
00009| `unstable_noStore` can be used to declaratively opt out of prerendering and indicate a particular component should not be cached.
00010| 
00011| ```jsx
00012| import { unstable_noStore as noStore } from 'next/cache';
00013| 
00014| export default async function ServerComponent() {
00015|   noStore();
00016|   const result = await db.query(...);
00017|   ...
00018| }
00019| ```
00020| 
00021| > **Good to know**:
00022| >
00023| > - `unstable_noStore` is equivalent to `cache: 'no-store'` on a `fetch`
00024| > - `unstable_noStore` is preferred over `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` as it is more granular and can be used on a per-component basis
00025| 
00026| - Using `unstable_noStore` inside [`unstable_cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache) will not opt out of static generation. Instead, it will defer to the cache configuration to determine whether to cache the result or not.
00027| 
00028| ## Usage
00029| 
00030| If you prefer not to pass additional options to `fetch`, like `cache: 'no-store'`, `next: { revalidate: 0 }` or in cases where `fetch` is not available, you can use `noStore()` as a replacement for all of these use cases.
00031| 
00032| ```jsx
00033| import { unstable_noStore as noStore } from 'next/cache';
00034| 
00035| export default async function ServerComponent() {
00036|   noStore();
00037|   const result = await db.query(...);
00038|   ...
00039| }
00040| ```
00041| 
00042| ## Version History
00043| 
00044| | Version   | Changes                                         |
00045| | --------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
00046| | `v15.0.0` | `unstable_noStore` deprecated for `connection`. |
00047| | `v14.0.0` | `unstable_noStore` introduced.                  |
00048|

00002| title: unstable_noStore
00003| description: API Reference for the unstable_noStore function.
00004| version: legacy
00005| ---
00006| 
00007| **In version 15, we recommend using [`connection`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) instead of `unstable_noStore`.**
00008| 
00009| `unstable_noStore` can be used to declaratively opt out of prerendering and indicate a particular component should not be cached.
00010| 
00011| ```jsx
00012| import { unstable_noStore as noStore } from 'next/cache';
00013| 
00014| export default async function ServerComponent() {
00015|   noStore();
00016|   const result = await db.query(...);
00017|   ...
00018| }
00019| ```
00020| 
00021| > **Good to know**:
00022| >
00023| > - `unstable_noStore` is equivalent to `cache: 'no-store'` on a `fetch`
00024| > - `unstable_noStore` is preferred over `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` as it is more granular and can be used on a per-component basis
00025| 
00026| - Using `unstable_noStore` inside [`unstable_cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache) will not opt out of static generation. Instead, it will defer to the cache configuration to determine whether to cache the result or not.
00027| 
00028| ## Usage
00029| 
00030| If you prefer not to pass additional options to `fetch`, like `cache: 'no-store'`, `next: { revalidate: 0 }` or in cases where `fetch` is not available, you can use `noStore()` as a replacement for all of these use cases.
00031| 
00032| ```jsx
00033| import { unstable_noStore as noStore } from 'next/cache';
00034| 
00035| export default async function ServerComponent() {
00036|   noStore();
00037|   const result = await db.query(...);
00038|   ...
00039| }
00040| ```
00041| 
00042| ## Version History
00043| 
00044| | Version   | Changes                                         |
00045| | --------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
00046| | `v15.0.0` | `unstable_noStore` deprecated for `connection`. |
00047| | `v14.0.0` | `unstable_noStore` introduced.                  |
00048|

events.content: Done. The page uses `connection()` from `next/server` (`app/page.tsx:4`) — the recommended approach in Next.js 15+ to opt out of static prerendering. The `await connection()` call tells Next.js to stop prerendering at that point, so `new Date()` and `Math.random()` produce fresh values on every request.
